I am just posting this so more people understand that it doesn't take a lot of space to grow stuff.

I would say you can get this harvest in about 10 to 12 square feet, provided you have good, high compost soil in your bed.

Potatoes - 2 large containers, about the size of a whiskey barrel

Tomatoes - one or two single stem plants - about 3 sq. ft.

Bell pepper - one plant - about 1 sq. ft.

Onions - you can cram a dozen onion plants in about 2 sq. ft. - they don't need much room. I plant onions as dividers between plants in my dense garden bed, so they're basically 'free' in terms of space needed. And there is a theory that their odor confuses pests from finding other plants.
